claims: NASA's most recent major crewed launch was the Artemis II mission.
The Artemis II mission lifted off on April 1, 2026.
The Artemis II mission lifted off from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39B in Florida.
The Artemis II crew consists of four astronauts.
The Artemis II crew is currently traveling to the Moon.
The Artemis II crew is traveling on the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
The Artemis II crew is traveling on the Orion spacecraft.
The mission goal of Artemis II is a crewed test flight around the Moon to test systems for future human lunar exploration.
The crew of Artemis II is Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The vehicle of Artemis II is the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
Before the current Artemis era, the last Space Shuttle mission was STS-135 (Atlantis).
STS-135 marked the end of the Space Shuttle program.
